differences.title: 1. Initial Load
differences.leftDesc: Reduces initial JavaScript payload, improving perceived performance and time-to-interactive.
differences.rightDesc: Requires shipping JavaScript to the client for rendering, increasing initial load times.

differences.title: 2. Interactivity
differences.leftDesc: Components can be interactive but require client-side hydration to attach event listeners.
differences.rightDesc: Components are interactive immediately after rendering in the browser.

differences.title: 3. Data Fetching
differences.leftDesc: Can fetch data directly on the server without exposing secrets or hitting API limits.
differences.rightDesc: Requires fetching data on the client, potentially exposing keys or facing CORS issues.

differences.title: 4. Bundle Size
differences.leftDesc: Significantly reduces the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser.
differences.rightDesc: Client components contribute to the overall JavaScript bundle size.

differences.title: 5. SEO
differences.leftDesc: Search engines can easily crawl and index content rendered on the server.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on JavaScript execution for rendering content, which some crawlers might struggle with.

differences.title: 6. State Management
differences.leftDesc: State managed on the server, less concern for client-side state synchronization.
differences.rightDesc: State is managed within the browser, requiring careful handling for updates and persistence.

differences.title: 7. Caching
differences.leftDesc: Leverages server-side caching strategies for improved performance and reduced load.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on browser caching mechanisms, which can be less granular and predictable.
